CORRECTION: The steps/scheduler cliff reported below (seed 42 only) turned out to be a single-seed artifact. Re-running the same step counts at seed 123 gives r = -0.69 (10 steps), -0.19 (15 steps), -0.32 (18 steps) -- poor at every step count, unlike seed 42 which was excellent at 10 and 15. Zeroing the scheduler's mandatory SDE noise term (CogVideoXDPMScheduler.step() adds randn noise regardless of eta -- eta is unused in the formula) made results WORSE (18 steps deterministic: only 3/49 frames had a recognizable rider), ruling out determinism as a fix. See README Part 3 for the full corrected writeup. Conclusion: no steps/CFG/scheduler configuration reliably controls motion-tracking quality in this setup; apparent differences are dominated by seed variance.

18step_dpm_cfg1_seed42_deterministic_no_.note: worse than stochastic version at the same step count -- noise term is load-bearing

seed42.note: reproducible across a repeat run (pixel-level non-identical, mean abs diff ~3.9/255, but same quality tier)

seed_sweep_at_10steps.summary: Of 4 distinct seeds tried at 10 steps/CFG1/DPM, only 1 (seed 42) gave a clearly good result (r>0.9); the other 3 ranged from mediocre to negative (r -0.69 to 0.12). Good tracking is not the default outcome of this configuration -- it is what happened to come out of one particular seed we used throughout the rest of the report, and reproducibility testing shows that seed genuinely and reliably does well (not just hardware noise on top of noise), it is just not representative of the configuration in general.

cfg3.0.note: best of the 3 CFG values tried on this seed

cfg_sweep_at_seed123_10steps.summary: CFG does not monotonically help: on the same bad seed (123), CFG=3 partially rescued tracking (r went from -0.69 to +0.38) but CFG=6 went back to bad (-0.42). Combined with the step-count and seed sweeps above, no single knob (steps, CFG, or scheduler type) has a monotonic, reliable effect on how well the generated video tracks the commanded trajectory in this NF4 + block-offload setup -- quality is highly sensitive to the exact combination of seed/steps/CFG in a way that looks close to chaotic, not a simple quality/speed tradeoff.
